Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE-2026-116319.title: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to e ...

Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

This wrongly allows the table owner to run DROP STATISTICS and ALTER STATISTICS via this improper ownership.  It wrongly denies those commands to the prior statistics object owner.  DROP TABLE remains able to remove statistics objects, so this exploit achieves nothing in many ownership arrangements.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

CVE-2026-6470.title: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL DDL commands allows an object ...
CVE-2026-6470.description: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL DDL commands allows an object creator to achieve denial of service against ALTER and DROP of the type, via creating a dependency on the type.  Many DDL operations did check the privilege, but assigning a range subtype and referencing the type from an SQL expression did not.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

CVE-2026-6474.title: Externally-controlled format string in PostgreSQL timeofday() fun ...
CVE-2026-6474.description: Externally-controlled format string in PostgreSQL timeofday() function allows an attacker to retrieve portions of server memory, via crafted timezone zones.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23 are affected.

CVE-2025-8713.title: PostgreSQL optimizer statistics allow a user to read sampled data ...
CVE-2025-8713.description: PostgreSQL optimizer statistics allow a user to read sampled data within a view that the user cannot access.  Separately, statistics allow a user to read sampled data that a row security policy intended to hide.  PostgreSQL maintains statistics for tables by sampling data available in columns; this data is consulted during the query planning process.  Prior to this release, a user could craft a leaky operator that bypassed view access control lists (ACLs) and bypassed row security policies in partitioning or table inheritance hierarchies.  Reachable statistics data notably included histograms and most-common-values lists.  CVE-2017-7484 and CVE-2019-10130 intended to close this class of vulnerability, but this gap remained.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17.6, 16.10, 15.14, 14.19, and 13.22 are affected.

CVE-2026-116303.title: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL type conversion allows a data ...
CVE-2026-116303.description: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL type conversion allows a database user to invoke a cast function despite lacking EXECUTE privilege on that function, via foreign keys, to_json(), and others.  A successful attack requires the attacker to search each database for access-restricted cast functions and identify confidentiality impact specific to each function implementation found.  There are few or no practical examples of an access-restricted cast function or of a cast function having confidentiality impact.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE-2026-116304.description: Use after free in PostgreSQL coordination of anonymous RECORD type identifiers among parallel workers allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via causing one process to free a shared tuple descriptor while another process retains and later uses its address. Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE-2026-116308.title: Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL dict_int allows a database user to ...

CVE-2026-116309.description: Type confusion in PostgreSQL plperl may allow an object creator to execute arbitrary code, via blessing a non-hash reference into PostgreSQL::InServer::ARRAY. Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

CVE-2026-116311.description: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL DROP OWNED allows a role to remove itself from restrictive row level security policies, thereby reading or modifying rows that the policy was intended to deny, via queries after the DROP OWNED. CVE-2026-116314.title: Improper input validation in PostgreSQL pg_restore allows a non-p ...
CVE-2026-116314.description: Improper input validation in PostgreSQL pg_restore allows a non-plain archive provider to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running pg_restore, via a crafted archive. Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE-2026-116318.title: SQL injection in PostgreSQL pg_dump allows an object creator to e ...
CVE-2026-116318.description: SQL injection in PostgreSQL pg_dump allows an object creator to execute arbitrary SQL as the user restoring the dump, via an inherited column having a child-local not-null constraint whose name requires quoting.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

CVE-2026-116319.title: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to e ...
CVE-2026-116319.description: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via reentrant return_next() calls.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE-2026-116320.title: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to e ...

CVE-2026-18447.title: Type confusion in PostgreSQL SQL-language functions allows an obj ...
CVE-2026-18447.description: Type confusion in PostgreSQL SQL-language functions allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via an output parameter of type "any".  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE-2026-6460.title: Type confusion in PostgreSQL allows an object creator to execute  ...
CVE-2026-6460.description: Type confusion in PostgreSQL allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via ALTER ... SET DATA TYPE primarily.  Other DDL attack routes exist, such as "ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN; ROLLBACK; ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN".  The system had inadequate tracking of typed values, and values were not self-identifying.  Stale values could appear in data dictionary entries, PL/pgSQL variables, and many other parts of the system.  PostgreSQL Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE-2026-6467.title: Uncontrolled search path element in PostgreSQL CREATE EXTENSION a ...
CVE-2026-6467.description: Uncontrolled search path element in PostgreSQL CREATE EXTENSION allows an attacker with database-level CREATE privilege to execute arbitrary code as the bootstrap superuser, via ALTER SCHEMA ... RENAME or CREATE EXTENSION ... SCHEMA "$user".  ALTER EXTENSION was also affected.  A trusted-extension script located the wrong object and executed arbitrary SQL of the attacker's choice.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE-2026-6469.title: Incorrect ownership assignment in PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE ALTER TY ...
CVE-2026-6469.description: Incorrect ownership assignment in PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE ALTER TYPE command reassigns ownership of dependent statistics objects to the current user.  This wrongly allows the table owner to run DROP STATISTICS and ALTER STATISTICS via this improper ownership.  It wrongly denies those commands to the prior statistics object owner.  DROP TABLE remains able to remove statistics objects, so this exploit achieves nothing in many ownership arrangements.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

CVE-2026-6470.title: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL DDL commands allows an object ...
CVE-2026-6470.description: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL DDL commands allows an object creator to achieve denial of service against ALTER and DROP of the type, via creating a dependency on the type.  Many DDL operations did check the privilege, but assigning a range subtype and referencing the type from an SQL expression did not.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.
